newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CC Amatil still keen on purchases.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CC Amatil still keen on purchases.

text.p: Beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd (CCA) said on Tuesday it would not rule out further acquisitions, although recent purchases have failed to lift its earnings outlook for 1996.

CCA managing director Norb Cole told reporters after he delivered a speech to the Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce that the group's parent Coca Cola Co was likely to continuing offering new Coke bottling franchises.
The bottler has been under investor pressure over the past two days following a profit warning last Friday when it said it expected 1996 profit to be little changed from last year.
"Acquisitions of Coke franchises are offered to 'anchor' bottlers when there is good business reason," Cole said.
"If it contiguous or if you are one of the best at developing the marketplace then you are offered the opportunity to acquire a neighbouring franchise," he said.

"That is still the same criteria and if and when the Coca-Cola Co want us to be the next franchisee for some new territory, then we are interested in doing that, but until then we are going to focus on our own markets," Cole said.
CCA has been very acquisitive over the past two years buying Coca-Cola bottling franchises mainly in Eastern Europe, which has been partly funded by new equity issues.
Cole said CCA was spending about A$800 million on capital expenditure in 1996, but he would not comment on 1997 spending.
The Coca-Cola Co owns about 36 percent of CCA.
At 3.55 p.m (0455 GMT), CCA shares were 25 cents or 2.26 percent lower at A$15.15 on a volume of 3.89 million shares.
